FN-DEVVHTN-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 62
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/13/2024
Senate Bill 62 as introduced would exempt the gross proceeds of the sale of certain baby
supplies, baby formula, maternity clothing, and menstrual hygiene products from sales and use
tax, which would decrease sales and use tax receipts annually to: (1) the Education Trust Fund
by an estimated $8.7 million; (2) the State General Fund by an estimated $2.5 million; and (3)
local governments by an estimated $15.2 million.
Pursuant to the provisions of the ETF Rolling Reserve Act contained in Section 29-9-3(b)(3),
Code of Alabama 1975, the provisions of this bill would reduce the ETF fiscal year
appropriation cap for fiscal year 2025 by $8.7 million.

FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 62
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/14/2024
Senate Bill 62 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education would exempt
the gross proceeds of the sale of certain baby supplies, baby formula, maternity clothing, and
menstrual hygiene products from state sales and use tax, which would decrease state sales and
use tax receipts annually to: (1) the Education Trust Fund by an estimated $8.7 million; and (2)
the State General Fund by an estimated $2.5 million.
Pursuant to the provisions of the ETF Rolling Reserve Act contained in Section 29-9-3(b)(3),
Code of Alabama 1975, the provisions of this bill would reduce the ETF fiscal year
appropriation cap for fiscal year 2025 by $8.7 million.

FN-DEVVHTN-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 62
Committee: Way and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/19/2024
Senate Bill 62 as passed the Senate would reduce sales tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund
by an estimated $10.3 million in Fiscal Year 2025 and $11.2 annually, beginning in Fiscal Year
2026 and each year thereafter, by exempting the gross proceeds of the sale of certain baby
supplies, baby formula, maternity clothing, and menstrual hygiene products from state sales and
use tax.

FN-DEVVHTN-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 62
Committee: Way and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/21/2024
Senate Bill 62 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would reduce sales
tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund by an estimated $10.3 million in Fiscal Year 2025 and
$11.2 annually, beginning in Fiscal Year 2026 and each year thereafter, by exempting the gross
proceeds of the sale of certain baby supplies, baby formula, maternity clothing, and menstrual
hygiene products from state sales and use tax.
This bill could also decrease sales tax receipts to local governments by a cumulative maximum
of $15.2 million annually, if all local governments adopted the exemption provided by this bill.
